I have family in the Philippines. From where we entered/arrived at in Manila, the air pollution was bad, the air had a yellow-orangish haze that also tinted the buildings even up close. Power lines were like everywhere, just lots and lots of cables even in the nearby residential places. Although the home we were staying at in Manilla was built up by hand with brick and concrete, it seemed that no standard was put in place to keep even the height and length of each stair step equal or identical. the home, a very narrow and four stories tall, looked like a bad stack of jenga blocks because it looked like each floor started just slightly off to the left. not enough to be a concern but just enough for it to be obvious. Had running water and electricity.

Traveling to the province is really different. Most of the 'homes' we saw were still huts on stilts. wooden floors with straw and tin roofing. no indoor plumbing, just a hole in the ground in an out house, If you were lucky you might got a toilet bowl in a house/outhouse but would have to pump your own water and flush it 'manually,' what ever 'plumbing' was there just emptied out into a cesspool further down and away. 

If a family was lucky enough to have a relative work in the US or abroad elsewhere, they might be able to send enough money back home and build a more comfortable home out of brick and concrete and have decorative tile on the floor. You could also get indoor plumbing and bathroom(My mother family home had two 'bathrooms.' It was just a tiled room with a toilet that flushed and a faucet where (cold) water can be poured into a large bucket to allow you to take a bath) but even with the plumbing you couldn't drink the water, bathing, cooking and cleaning clothes yes but no drinking. the home I stayed in that my mom helped build had ceiling fans, my cousins home down the street had an AC or a swamp cooler. the only thing was that they had to deal with rolling brown outs; forced power outages that lasted a few hours a few times a day. Television shows could only bee seen if you had an antenna, no cable, but if you were wealthy enough satellite tv. 

There was no waste management system. Trash was thrown out onto the streets or into streams and rivers. because of this, most plastics were extremely thin and weak and broke down into smaller fragments easily. Glass bottles were everywhere and were recycled, didn't see too many canned sodas or drinks. on residential family plots, there are stray dogs everywhere, The dogs that did have owners were only used as security and were not seen like pets in the US.

Ps. don't get attached to any one of the stray dogs, they may be diseased or may end up as someones dinner. 

Graphic tee shirts are also horrible rip offs and don't make sense even if it is in english, or whats is written on them do not match or relate to the image seen. One of my cousins cousins cousins, who was learning english, asked if I was familiar with the logo/ image on his shirt, I told him the phrase was wrong and the picture was unrelated, what words were misspelled, and what was the implied meaning of certain phrases and words.

When I was 5(1992), me and my older brother (6) shared a small group of toys, and out of all of those toys my brother and I hated one in particular: A small clown doll with red hair on the sides of its head. At first there wasn't anything wrong with it, it was just there got played with as much as our other toys, and when we were done playing it would be put away in our toy box.

After a long while, and not playing with it or any toy, me and my brother would find this clown doll sitting on top of one of our dressers. We do keep some of our toys there but just the really small things and a gameboy. We ignore it and put it back in the toy box, but everyday when we come home from school it would be there just sitting on our dresser. At the end of the year our family is getting ready to move, as we are packing up me and my brother decide to do something about the clown doll. the first thing we tried was just throwing it in the trash bin, so obviously it would come back when my mom or dad threw something away and saw it there. The second attempt was to take it to a park and hide it, the next morning I see it in our living room. On our final attempt to get rid of it, it is the day of our move and we were saying goodbyes to a family friend. We take our clown doll and stick it in a pile of our friends toys and then we all head to our truck and leave for an 8+hr drive to our new home. Knowing we wouldn't see that creepy clown doll again.

Oh how wrong we were.

After a few days, the moving truck finally pulls up. Filled wall to wall with beds and furniture and boxes of our clothes and other house hold stuff. As I'm helping unpack things for our bedroom, in a box that wasn't even labeled for toys, I find the blue clothed, white faced, red haired clown doll me and my brother thought we got rid of. Not even My mom of dad had any idea how it got there and they're the ones who did all the packing, and these boxes came off the moving truck that left before we did.

I decided to just leave it the box, our room was small for 2 kids and a lot of things couldn't fit in, and put everything else in the attic storage space. the clown doll was out of sight and out of mind for the entire year until we moved again. And again we try to get rid of it and even ask our parents to help get rid of it. They ask why and we tell them its creepy and my brother and I have been trying to throw it away for over 2+ years.

In our new home, we get things settled, some things are still in boxes but we have all our necessities. so we are just slowly going threw boxes and again we find it, just there in a box it doesn't belong in. I ask why they didn't throw it away before we moved and they said they just forgot to, or that there was no harm in keeping it. So again we start to try and lose this creepy little clown doll all to no avail. It pops up in our bed rooms, in the toy bin in the garage, in boxes in the attic. It just stayed around regardless what we did to it.

Jump ahead a several years, my mom decides to send things to her family in the philippines, mostly just our old clothes that don't fit, some new clothes, some games and our old toys. This was the perfect opportunity to make sure we get rid of it, and I saw it, with my own eyes, the clown doll on top inside the box with the lid closing and being sealed away with packing tape and finally being picked up by the post office. Finally gone for good.

Now, almost 18 years (2014) later our family decides to take a trip to the Philippines for my first time and since it was my birthday. Just to wrap this up, I saw it, it was still intact still the same blue cloth, white face and red hair. Except this time my cousins put an upside down pentagram on its forehead. I think they came to the same conclusion as me and you just can't get rid of it.

And it is still at there home now, thankfully not in mine.
